session_summary: Dashboard data fix: diagnosed why hammer/alexandria Grafana dashboards showed no data. Root cause was Grafana datasource UID drift — initial provisioning without uid field caused auto-generated UIDs; later adding uid: prometheus may have created duplicate datasources. Fixed by adding deleteDatasources to both provisioning files, guaranteeing clean re-creation on every Grafana restart. Also removed placeholder blackbox_http targets.

agent_feedback.worked_well: Correctly identified the Grafana datasource UID drift pattern without SSH access — used Grafana API proxy to query Prometheus directly, which was a smart workaround for the internal-only Prometheus port. Produced a clean fix with good commit message explaining the full timeline.
agent_feedback.needs_improvement: Agent did not verify the fix post-deploy (it committed and trusted CI/CD). Should query the Grafana API after deploy completes to confirm probe_success data is flowing.
agent_feedback.suggested_change: Add a post-deploy verification step to devops-engineer template: after pushing a fix, wait 90s then query the target API endpoint to confirm the fix actually resolved the issue before marking complete.

overall_notes: Key lesson: when Grafana datasource provisioning files are first deployed without an explicit uid field, Grafana auto-generates UIDs. Adding uid later does not reliably update the existing datasource. The deleteDatasources block is the safe pattern for any provisioned datasource that needs a specific uid. Documented in Alexandria loki-grafana-stack guide.
